sections.overview: This widespread Central and South American tree sloth belongs to Bradypus, the three-toed sloth genus; all four limbs bear three long claws.
sections.identification: Adults average about 58 cm long and 4.6 kg; a brown throat and face, long limbs and coarse green-tinged fur help identify it.
sections.habitat: It lives mainly in the canopy of tropical and subtropical forests, including rain forest, dry forest and swamp forest.
sections.diet: It is a strict herbivore, browsing leaves, flowers and fruit, often from Cecropia trees; plants provide much of its water.
sections.behavior: Slow movement and algae growing in the fur provide camouflage; it can swim and only occasionally descends to the ground.
sections.reproduction: Females generally give birth to one young after roughly six months of gestation, and the young clings to its mother while developing.
sections.ecology: It shares Bradypus with B. tridactylus and the more restricted B. torquatus; B. variegatus and B. tridactylus overlap near Manaus and documented hybrids caution against oversimplified identification.
sections.conservation: Globally assessed as Least Concern, it can still face local forest loss, road mortality, capture for pets and disturbance by tourism.
